statement: Two archers each shot $30$ arrows at a target. Both archers had a mean score of $7.8$ points per arrow. The standard deviation of archer X's scores was $0.6$ points, and the standard deviation of archer Y's scores was $1.9$ points. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by this information?

choices.text: Archer Y's total score was greater than archer X's total score.
choices.misconception: I thought a bigger standard deviation means bigger scores, so archer Y must have scored more points in total.

choices.text: Every one of archer X's scores was between $7.2$ and $8.4$ points.
choices.misconception: I thought every score has to lie within one standard deviation of the mean, so all of X's scores were within 0.6 of 7.8.

choices.text: Archer X and archer Y had the same median score.
choices.misconception: I thought that if two data sets have the same mean, they must also have the same median.

choices.text: Archer X's scores were, as a group, closer to $7.8$ points than archer Y's scores were.

hints: Standard deviation measures spread, not size.
A smaller standard deviation means the values tend to sit closer to the mean.
Both means are $7.8$, and X's standard deviation, $0.6$, is much smaller than Y's, $1.9$. What does that say about how far the scores fall from $7.8$?

solutions.reliable: Standard deviation describes how far values typically fall from the mean. Both archers have mean $7.8$, and archer X's standard deviation is smaller, so X's scores were more tightly clustered around $7.8$. The totals are equal ($30 \cdot 7.8 = 234$ for each), values can lie more than one standard deviation from the mean, and equal means do not force equal medians.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
